official_measurement_examples.name: Current TPO collection
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data reported 107,674 tree preservation orders from 74 providers with its collector last run on 24 July 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: Zone and tree separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data maintains separate tree-preservation-order, tree-preservation-zone and tree datasets, so the legal instrument and mapped tree or group geometry must not be collapsed into one record type.

official_measurement_examples.name: TPO work consent
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government planning guidance states a TPO can prohibit cutting down, topping, lopping, uprooting, wilful damage or destruction without the local planning authority's written consent, subject to legal exceptions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Roots included
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government guidance states cutting roots is treated as a prohibited activity for TPO purposes and can require authority consent.

official_measurement_examples.name: Appeal timing distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK allows appeal where protected-tree work is refused, conditioned or not decided within 8 weeks; after a decision the usual appeal deadline is 28 days.

official_measurement_examples.name: Conservation-area distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Trees in conservation areas can be protected through a separate notification regime even where no individual TPO exists, so absence of a TPO is not general permission to carry out tree works.

official_measurement_examples.name: Felling licence distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Forestry Commission's July 2026 felling guidance is a separate regime from TPO consent and planning permission; an applicable exemption or permission in one regime must not be presumed to satisfy another.

official_measurement_examples.name: Dataset completeness limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data notes parts of the national tree-control collection still include MHCLG-created data while authoritative local-source coverage is being expanded, so absence from the national collection is not definitive absence of protection.

core_rules: a TPO legal-instrument record is distinct from individual-tree or zone geometry
absence from the national Planning Data TPO collection is not proof no local TPO exists
TPO consent is not planning permission
planning permission does not automatically authorise works prohibited by a TPO
conservation-area tree controls can apply without an individual TPO
a felling licence is distinct from TPO consent
a TPO exception must not be presumed without matching current legal facts
tree replacement notices are distinct from consent to carry out the original work
appeal rights do not themselves authorise tree works
historic TPO records must retain confirmation variation revocation and date context
tree geometry does not determine land ownership or access rights
tree protection does not itself determine development capacity or dwelling yield
Planning Data legal-instrument and geometry records must not be silently deduplicated by proximity
tree work compliance does not replace ecology ancient-woodland or heritage controls
no parcel tree-control clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
